tasks.short: Move and position foundry workpieces with cranes or signals

steps.what: Check the actual workpiece, positioning requirement and readiness for the specific movement using the established lifting procedure
inputs: Actual mold section, pattern or bottom board
Established site procedure and actual movement conditions
outputs: Readiness check for the exact next movement or a decision to stop

steps.what: Operate the crane and position the workpiece when this worker is the designated operator
inputs: Existing crane controls, defined as OTHER
outputs: Workpiece moved and positioned under continuous human observation

steps.what: Signal another designated operator to move and position the workpiece when acting as the signaller
outputs: Human signals for the checked movement and observed positioning

tasks.design: Retain the existing physical process and its human readiness checks. No {OTHER} crane-control change or generated lifting instruction is proposed; operating and signalling remain separate human actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on physical position, actual movement conditions and coordination with the operator.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software mechanism is established by this task description that removes the worker's physical handling or signalling effort.
tasks.still_hard: Observe changing conditions and position fragile or heavy foundry workpieces accurately.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain situational awareness and coordinate the actual movement.

ambition.what: No supported change to this physical task.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: crane-assisted positioning and human signalling depend on the actual workpiece and movement conditions; existing crane mechanisms do not establish a new software saving.

assumptions: Unmeasured illustrative distribution of active focal-role effort across readiness, operator and signaller duties; the worker can perform different branches across a work period. The 55 and 25 weights are not claimed duty frequencies.
Another operator's crane time is outside focal-role baseline when this worker signals; it is neither eliminated nor treated as a free software producer.

The readiness check is the ordinary physical check for the exact next movement, not an added self-approval ceremony. Repeat s1 before the relevant s2 or s3 action whenever the workpiece, intended movement or conditions change; active checking and feedback time remain fully retained.

No record write, report, message transmission through a separate system or lookup is established by the task. Physical movement and live signals are explicitly separated; no administrative baseline is invented to produce a saving.
Existing crane controls and established procedures are already baseline. No new sensor, robotic handling or remote-control system is assumed.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points remain. Gross and net saving are zero; incremental work is explicitly zero because no change is proposed.
unknowns: Actual division of operator and signaller duties and current handling equipment
research_questions: Does observation establish any separate repetitive information handling that is genuinely part of this task?

already_counted.description: Ordinary readiness checking for the actual movements

incremental.description: No proposed software or process change, so no additional maintenance or review work

approvals.approved_version: Exact movement checked in s1 under the actual current conditions; any change requires a fresh readiness check
Exact movement checked in s1 before its signal; changed conditions or instructions require a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Readiness, crane operation and live signalling are all retained; no documented information-handling step or new labour-removing mechanism supports a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

skills_to_grow: Maintain established lifting and signalling competence
role.ambitious_version: The foundry worker retains physical movement and positioning responsibilities; no software expansion is supported by this task alone.
